key_insight: IRT can be useful for AI benchmarks, but its rankings and item estimates become unreliable when benchmark conditions differ from the human-testing regime it was designed for.
engineering_relevance: Benchmark designers and evaluation engineers should check sample size, model distribution shape, and estimator scalability before trusting IRT-based capability estimates or item diagnostics.
method: Simulated response matrices from six widely used LLM benchmarks under three common IRT models.
Compared four IRT estimation approaches: marginal maximum likelihood, MCMC, variational inference, and a neural pseudo-Siamese estimator.
Evaluated feasibility, scalability, model ranking accuracy, performance prediction, and item-parameter reliability across 18,000 conditions.
evidence_signal: Across 18,000 simulation conditions, classical methods sometimes became computationally infeasible, while scalable methods could still produce unstable rankings and item-level inferences for small or nonnormal model sets.
watch_item: IRT outputs can look statistically precise even when the benchmark’s model count and capability distribution violate the assumptions under which the estimator is reliable.
paper_title: Can We Trust Item Response Theory for AI Evaluation?
